items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He studied with Frank Epstein, classical drumming

ctx.x: As for my wife, we met in Cincinnati when I was in the orchestra and therefore teaching at the conservatory there. I taught horn. She was – we were both 17. She was a student and a double major, piano and voice. I was on the faculty. We got together, and we were together 50 years. We first lived in New York, until I came to the Conservatory. I always said to Margie, if we ever leave New York, there’s only two places we can possible go. One is Boston, because of its cultural life and its history, and as an…

He was, as I say, not involved with music. He didn’t like school, and he cut a lot of classes. I didn’t know that. I just found out later. I was very upset. One day, he was – there was a music class led by a cellist here in Boston, a teacher who taught almost all the subjects and had a little orchestra also. All those schools in those days had orchestras. Most of them have disappeared nowadays. Edwin was standing out in the corridor, listening to the music in the room. As I say, he didn’t know anything about…

absorbed all this, and at some point it just came out almost full-fledged and not in any sort of stumbling, groping way, or “I hate to practice” or all that stuff, which almost always happens. These people – I didn’t have to tell them to practice. They – Edwin practiced 7, 8, 9 hours every day.
